# Two rules read from one share lock together

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`two-rules-lock-together` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](two-rules-lock-together.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> Two rules each read as a monotone function of one share are read so together; where selection under both favouring does not lower the share and both favour at every share, the pair is locked from the step after the first reading step.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. Two orders on rules compared together, and two rules each read from the share; each read monotonically, the pair is read monotonically. (`Becoming.RuleCapture.pairOrder`, `Becoming.RuleCapture.pairReading`, `Becoming.RuleCapture.ReadsShare.pair`)
2. From a start whose two rules favour, the share falls at no step and the pair is locked from the step after the first reading step. (`Becoming.RuleCapture.pair_locks`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- No axiom; the premises of favouring_locks for the pair: selection under both favouring does not lower the share, each rule read monotonically from the share and favouring at every share.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- That any actual rule is read from the share it selects, or that a second rule is.

**Standard boundaries:** No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used. · Contains no ethical predicate and evaluates neither arising nor ceasing. · Stated for discrete steps. · A law of the formal model; its correspondence to actual systems is a separate obligation. · Names follow the structural naming criteria and are adopted only where the statement has their exact meaning; readings are interpretations, open to revision. · A relation omitted by a weaker description does not refute the fuller account.
